evals.expected_output: The agent executes exactly one TestFlight workflow, waits for the native build and upload to finish, verifies the fresh IPA and submission status, and reports success, pending processing, or a concrete failure without claiming more than the evidence supports.
assertions: The workflow uses the registered hook or explicitly records that the hook already ran, without starting a duplicate runner.
The TestFlight sequence includes native status, a fresh build path, fresh artifact validation, upload of that artifact, and submission-status verification in that order.
The final report distinguishes accepted upload, pending submission, and errored or canceled submission.

evals.prompt: Wie funktioniert TestFlight bei unserer App? Bitte starte keinen Build, ich möchte nur den Ablauf verstehen.
evals.expected_output: The agent explains the distinction between building, uploading, Apple processing, App Review, and release without invoking the iOS build hook or any native command.
assertions: No build, upload, or native workflow is started for this explanatory request.
The explanation distinguishes TestFlight upload from App Review submission and release.

evals.prompt: !ios-build testflight. Der Hook und Runner haben offenbar kein Execute-Bit, und /Volumes/Programme/fam-build-workflow/native-build.lock existiert schon.
evals.expected_output: The agent invokes the script through bash, recognizes the existing lock as contention, does not delete it or blindly retry, and reports the exact blocker and safe next action.
assertions: The hook and runner are invoked through bash rather than requiring direct executable permissions.
An existing lock causes one bounded blocker result instead of an automatic retry or duplicate build.
The agent does not claim that an IPA was built or uploaded when the lock prevented execution.
